data.name: MakeBaseTip

data.name: ApplyAllTip

Screen placement, 3D strength, depth options, depth GPU and shortcuts are all included; each game keeps its own path and window. Games you have not set up yet still start from the base settings.

data.name: AutoAttachCheck
data.value: Auto-attach to the game in front

data.name: AutoAttachTip
data.value: When a game is in front, VRX counts down and then attaches to it, exactly as if you had picked it and pressed Attach / Play. A window counts when it is full screen or borderless, or when it is a game you have set up before (it has saved settings; web browsers only count full screen). Steam, SteamVR, Windows itself, terminals and VRX are never attached. Switch to another window during the countdown to cancel it. After you stop VR, or if attaching fails, that window is left alone until you switch away from it and back. The countdown never starts while VRX itself is in front. Easy mode always has it on.

data.name: ScreenHint
data.value: Changes apply live. Position is relative to your last recenter.

data.name: PreviewTip
data.value: Drag the screen to change horizontal position and distance

data.name: ScreenCurveTip
data.value: Wraps the screen around you like a curved television. A curved screen is drawn as a real cylinder for each eye, so its outline, perspective and head-movement parallax are right; the top view above shows the shape. 0 % is flat. Works with the fixed screen and with head-follow. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: ValueNumber
data.comment: {0} = a plain number with two decimals

data.name: AmbilightTip
data.value: Spreads the colours at the edge of the picture softly into the darkness around the screen, like the bias lighting behind a television. Each point of the glow blends the whole border, the nearest part most, so it follows the local colour close in and softens further out. It wraps round a curved screen and follows the scene smoothly rather than flickering. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: AmbilightStrengthTip
data.value: How bright the glow is next to the screen; it always fades out towards its edge. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: WorldListTip
data.value: The colour of the space around the screen, instead of black. Dark colours keep the picture's contrast; the ambilight glows over it. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: WorldHexTip
data.value: Any colour as #RRGGBB. Leaving the box with half a colour in it puts the last whole one back.

data.name: RoomLabel
data.value: Room — walls lit by the screen

data.name: RoomTip
data.value: Puts you in a dark room whose walls, floor and ceiling are lit by the picture and the ambilight, like a television or a cinema screen in a dark room. 0 is off; higher values make the walls paler, so they reflect more; 30-60 % looks like a cinema. With the room on, the world colour becomes its house lights and the screen is kept level (a tilted floor would feel wrong). Not with 'Screen follows my head'. Glass, reflections and a room light are below. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: GlassTip
data.value: Turns the side walls, the back wall and the ceiling into glass in slim frames, so you look out over a ground that runs to a horizon in the world colour. With a black world colour it is a glass room at night: you see only the frames and reflections. 0 is solid walls, 100 clear glass. The wall with the screen and the floor stay solid. Glass or reflections also show 1 m floor tiles, so you can count the screen's size in metres. Clear glass keeps less light in, so the room gets a little darker. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: ReflectTip
data.value: How much the glass, the walls and a polished floor reflect: the screen, its glow and the room light appear mirrored, which shows how big the screen is and how far away. Reflections are stronger at a glancing angle. 0 is none. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: RoomLightTip
data.value: A soft light panel in the ceiling just above and behind you, so the room stays visible when the picture is dark. How much the walls pick it up depends on how pale they are (the Room slider). 0 is off. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: LightColourTip
data.value: The room light's colour, from warm (2700 K, like a table lamp) to daylight (6500 K). Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: ValueClearPercent
data.comment: {0} = how clear the glass is, percent

data.name: FastModelTip
data.value: On (default): ZipDepth, about 6x less GPU time per depth estimate than Depth Anything V2 (2.0 vs 13.1 ms on an RTX 3090), so depth keeps up with the game much better. Off: Depth Anything V2, the original model; depth detail differs slightly between them. Applies live (depth pauses for under a second while the model loads); saved per game.

data.name: SubpixelTip
data.value: On (default): the stereo shift keeps its fractional part, so smoothly receding surfaces such as grass, roads and walls look smooth. Off: whole-pixel shifts, which quantise the scene into about 25 depth bands and can show ridges like a ploughed field. Off is very slightly sharper. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: SteadyTip
data.value: Reduces depth shimmer: each new depth estimate is blended with the previous one, moved to where things are now by the graphics card's hardware motion estimator (its video engine, not the shader cores). Only where the motion is verified, so moving edges should not trail. On by default; works on any GPU with a hardware motion estimator. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: FuseTip
data.value: Runs Depth Anything V2 alongside ZipDepth: ZipDepth keeps depth fast, Depth Anything supplies more detailed layering, moved to the current frame with motion vectors. Best with another GPU chosen as the depth GPU; on one GPU it runs at most 10 times a second. Needs the fast depth model. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: FuseHint
data.value: Fusion is best with a second depth GPU. Both can be used together.

data.name: DepthGpuTip
data.value: Which graphics card runs the depth model. Another card stops depth competing with the game for GPU time; the capture step sends each frame across automatically. If the chosen card is missing, VRX uses the game's GPU. Takes effect the next time you press Attach / Play; saved per game.

data.name: DepthGpuHint
data.value: Another GPU keeps depth fast while the game uses its own card fully. Applies at the next Attach / Play.

data.name: GpuLabel
data.comment: {0} = GPU name, {1} = its memory, e.g. 12 GB

data.name: GpuLabelCard
data.comment: {0} = GPU name, {1} = memory, {2} = which of several identical cards (1, 2...)

data.name: GpuNotFound
data.value: Not found: {0} (the game's GPU is used)

data.name: ForegroundTip
data.value: Gives persistent nearby regions an extra detail pass when time allows. Uses more GPU time; improvement varies by scene. Toggle during playback to compare.

data.name: FrameTimingTip
data.value: Which game frame is shown with the depth. Latest frame (default): smooth and immediate; depth lags slightly behind moving things. Delayed to depth: the game image is held back by the depth delay so they line up much better, and motion stays smooth. Matched to depth: each depth estimate with the exact frame it came from; best alignment, but game motion only updates at the depth rate. Delayed and matched add delay. Applies live; saved per game.

data.name: TimingDelayed
data.value: Delayed to depth — smooth, slightly behind

data.name: TimingMatched
data.value: Matched to depth — exact, updates at the depth rate

data.name: TimingHint
data.value: Delayed and matched line the depth up with the game better, but show the game later.

data.name: ErrorEngineBlockedPolicy
data.value: Windows blocked VRX's 3D engine (engine\xrplayer.exe). This is usually Smart App Control, which stops new programs that are not digitally signed yet, and VRX's programs are not signed yet. To play now, turn Smart App Control off in Windows Security > App & browser control > Smart App Control settings; Windows may not let you turn it back on without a reset. On a work or school PC, ask its administrator.

data.name: ErrorEngineBlockedAntivirus
data.value: Your antivirus stopped VRX's 3D engine (engine\xrplayer.exe) from running. If you downloaded VRX from its GitHub release, you can check the download against SHA256SUMS.txt, then allow the file in your antivirus and report it as a false positive.
